{{Quote|But you know all that is Kesh came from the ''Skyborn''. Nothing can be born of Kesh anew!|Izri Dazh, to Adari Vaal|<ref name="skyborn" />}}
'''Izri Dazh''' was a [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] member of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh's]] ruling [[Neshtovar]], active in the era of the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]]. Although considered to be quite aged by the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], Dazh led the Neshtovar as the High [[Council]]or, presiding over the [[Circle Eternal]] in the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Tahv]].

In 5,000 BBY, Dazh presided over hearings regarding supposedly heretical teachings by [[Geologist/Legends|geologist]] [[Adari Vaal]], that presented a view of Kesh's creation that ran contrary to the prevalent Keshiri [[Skyborn|religion]] of which Dazh was a devout follower. The sessions were heated, but they were interrupted by a sudden explosion in the nearby [[Takara Mountains|Cetajan Mountains]], which Dazh and the other Keshiri took as a sign from the Keshiri [[Deity/Legends|gods]], the Skyborn.

Harassment from Dazh and other Keshiri drove Adari Vaal to flee into the mountains, where she found the source of the explosion&mdash;a group of crash-landed [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]. Through Vaal's assistance, the Sith made their way into civilization, where they claimed to be the Skyborn. Although initially skeptical, Dazh became completely convinced of their divinity and grew devoted to serving the supposed Skyborn. With the Sith firmly entrenched as rulers of Kesh, Dazh eventually [[Death/Legends|died]] sometime before [[4975 BBY]], his religious faith seemingly affirmed.

==Biography==
{{Quote|You didn't believe them when they levitated your cane.''"<br />"''That ended when they levitated ''me''.|Adari Vaal and Izri Dazh, discussing the arrival of the purported Skyborn|<ref name="skyborn" />}}
[[File:Tahv.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Dazh held court in the city of Tahv.]]
Izri Dazh was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]], a native of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]], who was a high-ranking member of the world's [[Neshtovar]] ruling council. A veteran rider of Kesh's native [[uvak]] beasts by the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], Dazh was considered to be aged at that point in his life&mdash;he had developed a physical ailment that caused him to hobble, forcing him to use a [[Cane/Legends|cane]]&mdash;and had risen to the position of High [[Council]]or, presiding over the Neshtovar's court at the [[Circle Eternal]] in the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Tahv]].<ref name="skyborn" />

That year, Dazh and the Neshtovar presided over a major issue. [[Geologist/Legends|Geologist]] [[Adari Vaal]] had uncovered evidence that the land of Kesh had been formed naturally by the planet's [[Volcano/Legends|volcanoes]], contradicting the prevalent Keshiri [[Skyborn|religion]]. Dazh had a connection to her family, as he had eulogized her husband [[Zhari Vaal|Zhari]], a member of the Neshtovar, after he was [[Death/Legends|killed]] in an uvak-riding accident. After teaching her findings to geology students, Vaal was called before the Neshtovar. A devout religious man, Dazh directly confronted her about her teachings in a series of public hearings. During one particular hearing, Vaal presented physical evidence in the form of "flamestones" gathered from all across Kesh, Dazh refused to accept her protests, and accused her of being a heretic. Furthermore, Dazh hinted that Vaal's teachings could ultimately bring harm upon all the Keshiri by bringing upon the wrath of their [[Deity/Legends|gods]], the Skyborn. Suddenly, a massive, fiery explosion rocked the nearby [[Takara Mountains|Cetajan Mountains]], the force of which threw Dazh to the ground. He was helped to his feet by Vaal, confident that the Skyborn had sent them a message.<ref name="skyborn" />

[[File:Yaru_Korsin.jpg|thumb|left|175px|Dazh opened his home to the Sith Yaru Korsin, who he believed to be a god.]]
The meeting adjourned after the incident, as Dazh quibbled with his colleagues about what the explosion meant. By the next day, even though the still-burning mountain had been determined not to pose any threat to Tahv, the focus turned to Adari Vaal as a large mob formed in front of her home. Dazh joined the group and tried to speak with Vaal, but the woman was spooked by the mob's torches and fled on the back of her late husband's [[Nink (uvak)|uvak]], evading Neshtovar riders as she made her way into the mountains. Vaal discovered a group of [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] that had crash-landed in the Cetajan range&mdash;the source of the previous explosion&mdash;and aided them in reaching the mainland. Upon their arrival in Tahv, they claimed to be the Skyborn. Dazh was initially skeptical, but he was convinced of their divinity after being [[Telekinesis/Legends|levitated]] through [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="skyborn" />

Afterward, Dazh humbly greeted their leader, [[Yaru Korsin]], in the Circle Eternal in front of thousands of Keshiri and officially proclaimed them to indeed be their gods. With the Skyborn returned to Keshiri society, their members were quartered in the homes of the Neshtovar, with Korsin and his wife [[Seelah Korsin|Seelah]] residing in Dazh's domicile. In order to show devotion, Dazh declared that all Neshtovar, including himself, should move to humbler homes.<ref name="skyborn" /> Dazh died sometime before [[4975 BBY]], and his former home was used as a meeting-place for the [[Keshiri resistance]]&mdash;including some of Dazh's sons and grandsons&mdash;that opposed the rule of the Sith.<ref name="savior" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Your words glorify the Otherside, Adari Vaal. It's why you are here. You are here for preaching&mdash;''"<br />"''Teaching!''"<br />"''&mdash;telling these ''lies'' about the Great Battle to your acolytes!|Izri Dazh and Adari Vaal|<ref name="skyborn" />}}
[[File:Adari_Vaal.jpg|thumb|right|175px|The traditional Dazh strongly opposed the iconoclastic beliefs of fellow Keshiri Adari Vaal.]]
Izri Dazh was a devoutly religious individual, and very slow to accept any notion that contradicted his prior beliefs. Dazh rejected anything that went against the common religious beliefs in any way, and was even skeptical when presented with the purported Skyborn gods. Dazh was especially dismissive of Adari Vaal and her geologic teachings, regarding her as a heretic. In fact, Vaal's ideas provoked Dazh into outright rage in her hearings before the Neshtovar, and he constantly railed against her and her beliefs. Dazh felt his faith justified with the arrival of the Sith, and his initial skepticism gave way to devotion and subservience to the supposed Skyborn.<ref name="skyborn" />

Dazh had [[Color/Legends|lavender]] skin, and by 5,000 BBY, as an aged man, had gone completely bald. Dazh also suffered from a physical ailment which caused him to hobble when he walked, forcing him to make use of a cane.<ref name="skyborn" />

==Behind the scenes==
Izri Dazh first appeared in ''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Skyborn]]'', a [[2009]] [[eBook]] by [[John Jackson Miller]].<ref name="skyborn" />
